full_text:
You must file an opposition to the proposed dismissal
within the time period that is outlined in the letter
uploaded on the ACMS state hearing portal to
prevent the hearing from getting dismissed. Be sure
to counter with your strongest points!

Opposition to Proposed Dismissal

RE: SHN-SES

E-. DOCUMENTED ADMISSION OF DEFAULT (PORTAL ENTRY 05/04/2026)]
The Proposed Dismissal alleges there has been "no denial," which is factually contradicted
by the official portal record. Exhibit 04292026_lacare_letter . pdf (uploaded 05/04/2026)
contains L.A. Care Health Plan's written admission that they defaulted on the April 26
statutory deadline. Furthermore, the record documents L.A. Care's attempt to execute an
illegal, retroactive extension to May 10, 2026, after the initial 30-day window had already
expired. A dismissal based on a pending "review status" is invalid when the Health Plan has
already codified its default in writing.

I 2. STATUTORY SUPERIORITY OF AB 3275 (2024)]

The Proposed Dismissal's reliance on APL 07-002 (2007) is legally obsolete. Under Assembly
Bill 3275, effective January 1, 2026, the mandatory adjudication window for this claim is
strictly 30 calendar days.

+ Claim Received: March 27, 2026 (Verified via USPS Certified Mail).

* Statutory Deadline: April 26, 2026.

+ Current Status: 30 days in statutory default.
Failure to pay, contest, or deny within this 30-day window constitutes an administrative
inaction and a "denial by operation of law," compelling immediate appellate review.

B. EXHAUSTION MANDATE PER LASC CASE 26AVSC00192 |
On May 22, 2026, the Los Angeles Superior Court specifically deferred this matter to
administrative exhaustion under Government Code section 905. The Court has legally
mandated this venue for adjudication. Dismissing this hearing obstructs a direct judicial
directive, effectively denying the claimant access to the mandated administrative remedies
necessary to resolve a documented $2,307.00 financial default.

[. CLINICAL URGENCY & LIFE-THREATENING RISK]
Portal entries dated 05/03/2026 contain formal Medical Necessity Statements warning that
financial barriers to this specific treatment carry a "clinically significant risk of seizures and
life-threatening complications." The Department's attempt to delay adjudication for an
additional 120 days using superseded 2007 guidelines demonstrates a willful disregard for
documented patient safety and life-critical medical necessity.

CONCLUSION

I formally request that this Proposed Dismissal be vacated and a hearing be scheduled
immediately. The administrative record already contains the Health Plan's written admission
of default; there is no remaining “review” process other than the calculation of interest and
penalties mandated under AB 3275.

Nicolas Hernandez
